handoff.purpose: Evidence and record types, claim extraction parser.

symbols.name: Evidence
symbols.note: Dataclass holding evidence paths and files; provides refs() and text_tokens(); classmethods from_patch_artifact, from_files, from_text.

symbols.name: Evidence.refs
symbols.note: Returns tuple of evidence_ref(path, sha256 of exact bytes) for each file.

symbols.name: Evidence.text_tokens
symbols.note: Returns sum of count_tokens for each file text.

symbols.name: Evidence.from_patch_artifact
symbols.note: Classmethod constructing Evidence from a PatchArtifact-like object; uses getattr with defaults.

symbols.name: Evidence.from_files
symbols.note: Reads files from disk; unreadable files are named with <<UNREADABLE: ...>> placeholder.

symbols.name: Evidence.from_text
symbols.note: Constructs Evidence from a single text string.

symbols.name: Claim
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass for a single claim, verbatim, with checkable flag and optional check.

symbols.name: TurnRef
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass for a chained turn with status, reason, content, flags, latency.

symbols.name: ParticipantRecord
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass for roster accounting of a participant.

symbols.name: CouncilRecord
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass for council output; advisory by construction; provides checkable_claims, quorum, claims_by_author, render.

symbols.note: Validates advisory is True and ended is in END_REASONS.

symbols.name: CouncilRecord.quorum
symbols.note: Property returning a string with responded/requested and distinct_classes.

symbols.note: Returns dict mapping author to tuple of claims, sorted by author.

symbols.note: Splits content into claims; if no claim lines, returns a single parsed=False Claim; otherwise continues (truncated in chunk).

claims.text: ``author_vendor`` names the vendor that WROTE the material, so a council seat held by that same vendor is flagged ``self_review`` on every one of its turns.
claims.why: The docstring describes behaviour of seating/turn creation, not visible in this chunk; no code here sets self_review based on author_vendor.

claims.text: Evidence citations: path + sha256 of the EXACT bytes shown.
claims.why: refs() computes evidence_ref(path, (text or '').encode('utf-8','replace')) for each file, so the digest is over the exact bytes shown.

claims.text: Two participants citing "the file" may have been shown different bytes; without the digest the transcript records a citation nobody can reproduce.
claims.why: The digest is computed from the exact text bytes, so different bytes produce different digests; refs() includes that digest.
The method accepts an artifact and uses getattr to extract fields, consistent with that input type.

claims.text: ``changed_paths`` becomes the path channel; the diff itself is shown as one evidence file so the content channel scans it whole-file, per the floor's own contract.
claims.why: The method sets paths from changed_paths and files to (('PATCH.diff', diff),), exactly as described.

claims.text: Read files off disk as evidence. Unreadable files are NAMED, never silently dropped -- a missing evidence file that reads as an empty one is a council reviewing something other than what it says it reviewed.
claims.why: On OSError, the file is added with content '<<UNREADABLE: ...>>', so it is named and not dropped.

claims.text: ``checkable`` is true only when the author supplied a concrete deterministic check -- a command, a test, a specific line assertion.
claims.why: Claim has field checkable: bool = False and check: str = ''; the parser (later in file) sets checkable based on presence of a check, but within this chunk the field is as described.

claims.text: A claim without one is still recorded verbatim, and still counts for nothing on its own.
claims.why: Claim stores verbatim text; checkable_claims property only returns those with checkable=True, so non-checkable claims are recorded but not part of the runnable queue.

claims.text: The council's output. ADVISORY. It promotes nothing.
claims.why: CouncilRecord has advisory: bool = True and __post_init__ raises if advisory is not True; no fields for majority/score/approval.

claims.text: There is deliberately no majority, no score, no consensus and no approve/reject field, and none may be added: a caller must not be able to destructure a decision out of this object.
claims.why: The dataclass fields do not include any such decision fields; advisory is enforced True.

claims.text: What is here instead is every claim with its author and its evidence, the checkable subset, and honest roster accounting.
claims.why: Fields include claims, participants, turns, and derived views checkable_claims and claims_by_author.

claims.text: Always True and enforced. This object is evidence, not a decision.
claims.why: advisory defaults to True and __post_init__ raises if not True.

claims.text: The queue the gate can actually run.
claims.why: Property filters claims to those with checkable=True.

claims.text: ``"2 of 4 (2 distinct weight families)"`` -- never a bare fraction. "3 of 4" and "2 of 2" must not be able to render as the same thing.
claims.why: quorum returns f"{responded} of {requested} responded, {distinct_classes} distinct weight family/families", which includes distinct_classes and never a bare fraction.

claims.text: Human rendering. The degraded flag sits ADJACENT TO THE FINDINGS -- never in a footer, where a reader takes a two-vendor council for four.
claims.why: The render method places '*** DEGRADED ***' on the quorum line, which is near the top. The claim about 'adjacent to findings' and 'never in a footer' concerns layout relative to findings; findings are not explicitly rendered in this chunk, so full verification is not possible.

claims.text: A vendor that ignores the format is NOT summarised and NOT dropped: its whole answer becomes one ``parsed=False`` claim. Summarising dissent is the failure this module exists to avoid, so the parser never paraphrases.
claims.why: The code checks for claim line starts; if none, returns a single Claim with parsed=False and text=content (the whole answer). No summarisation occurs.

observations.what: Evidence.from_files uses Path.read_text with errors='replace', so unreadable bytes are replaced rather than raising; combined with OSError catch, unreadable files are named but content may be lossy.
Evidence.from_patch_artifact uses getattr with defaults; if artifact is None or lacks attributes, it silently produces empty paths/files rather than failing.
CouncilRecord.quorum does not pluralize 'family' based on count; always says 'family/families'.
_parse_claims is truncated mid-function; the rest of the parsing logic (how checkable is determined, how claims are split) is not visible in this chunk.
